Seminar Details

Seminar Title:

Development of an Adsorbent using Modified Industrial Waste for Treatment of Selenium-Containing Wastewater in Coal Mines

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Mining Engineering

Speaker Name:

Pallavi Behera ( Rollno : 519mn1004)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Room, Department of Mining Engineering

Date and Time:

15 Jul 2026 09.15 Hrs

Contact:

Himanshu Bhushan Sahu

Abstract:

Selenium (Se) toxicity due to mining is an emerging concern worldwide. Traces of selenium were found in some mine sumps of the Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields in Odisha. Selenium toxicity can degrade ecosystems and impact human health. In humans, prolonged exposure may cause changes in fingernails, brittleness, gastrointestinal disorders, skin rashes, and neurological irregularities, while in aquatic organisms, it may induce developmental malformations, reproductive impairment, and larval deformities, thereby threatening aquatic biodiversity. Systematic batch experiments were conducted to investigate the effects of various process parameters on selenium removal by the prepared adsorbents. Optimal performance was observed with 20 g/L dosages and 120 min by dolochar 10 g/L dosages and 90 min by FeD 20 g/L dosages and 120 min by DAl 10 g/L dosages and 90 min by FeBac 20 g/L dosages and 90 min by FeBD. Bacillus selenatarsenatis 9470T removed 99 % at 10 Se-mg/L, pH 6, 4 % inoculum (v/v) within 20 h. Bacillus selenatarsenatis 9470T showed a high maximum adsorption capacity, followed by FeBac, FeD, DAl, dolochar, and FeBD. The experimental data of dolochar, FeD, and Bacillus selenatarsenatis 9470T best fit the Langmuir isotherm, suggesting monolayer adsorption and physisorption, whereas FeBac and FeBD fit the Freundlich isotherm. The Temkin and Dubinin-Radushkevich models also showed good agreement with the experimental data. Kinetic analysis confirmed that selenium removal followed pseudo-second-order kinetics, indicating chemisorption. Moreover, the intraparticle diffusion model suggested the process involvement of multiple rate-limiting stages. The thermodynamic study showed that negative Gibbs free energy values increased for all prepared adsorbents, confirming the spontaneity of the process with increasing temperature, whereas Bacillus selenatarsenatis showed spontaneity up to 308 K thereafter, the negativity decreased with increasing temperature. Dolochar, FeD, and DAl showed endothermic and high randomness, whereas Bacillus selenatarsenatis 9470T, FeBac, and FeBD showed exothermic and low randomness. Techno-economic analysis identified FeBac and FeBD as the most profitable adsorbents, exhibiting the highest NPVs (USD 363.79 and 417.66), IRRs (46.5% and 39%), and RORs, while FeBac, DAl, and FeD remained profitable at only 19&ndash20% capacity compared to the higher BEPs of FeBD (64.3%) and bacterial biomass (46.93%).
